pricing.faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
pricing.faq.card.q: Do I need a credit card to start?
pricing.faq.card.a: No. The Community plan is free forever and requires no payment details. The Pro trial also starts without a card.
pricing.faq.eventPass.q: What exactly does an Event Pass cover?
pricing.faq.eventPass.a: One competition, for as long as it’s running. The pass ({pass}) gives that competition 10 divisions and 128 entrants per division. You also get advanced formats, exports and realtime, a one-time AI credit top-up (+5 AI credits), and a 3% platform fee on its entry fees instead of Community’s 5% — and it stops counting against your free active-competition slot. A competition holds one pass and keeps it. Your club logo and card entry fees work on every plan already, pass or no pass. Other competitions in your org stay on Community limits.
pricing.faq.upgraded.q: I bought an Event Pass and later went Pro — what happens?
pricing.faq.upgraded.a: While you're on Pro, Pro's limits apply across the whole organisation — and on the competition you passed, the two are read together: whichever limit is higher wins, so nothing the pass bought is taken back. If you ever cancel Pro the pass carries that competition on its own, for as long as it is still running — a pass is tied to the competition it was bought for and stops with it.
pricing.faq.trialEnd.q: What happens when my Pro trial or subscription ends?
pricing.faq.trialEnd.a: Your org drops back to Community limits automatically. Nothing is deleted — competitions over the limit become read-only until you archive down to quota or upgrade again.
pricing.faq.fees.a: Yes, on every plan — Community included. What your plan buys is a cheaper cut: the platform fee is 5% on Community, 3% on a competition with an Event Pass, 2% on Pro. Connect your club's Stripe account and fees from online registration are paid out directly to the club.
pricing.faq.platformFee.q: What's the platform fee, and is it on top of Stripe's own fees?
pricing.faq.platformFee.a: It's {communityFee}% on Community, {passFee}% with an Event Pass, {proFee}% on Pro — charged on your paid entry fees. It's additive, not instead of Stripe: your club's connected Stripe account still pays Stripe's own processing fees on every charge, on top of our cut. Connect your club's Stripe account and payouts go straight to the club.
pricing.faq.groups.q: Can one subscription cover more than one organisation?
pricing.faq.groups.a: Yes. A subscription is a billing group: it can hold several organisations under one card and one invoice, and each organisation after the first costs no more than half your plan’s rate. Every organisation in the group runs on the group’s plan, so joining a Pro group takes an organisation’s entry-fee rate from 5% to 2%. Payouts are untouched — each organisation keeps its own Stripe account and its own bank details.
pricing.faq.currencies.q: Which currencies can I pay in?
pricing.faq.currencies.a: USD, EUR, GBP and INR — use the switcher above. Your first checkout pins the currency for future renewals.
pricing.faq.annual.a: Yes — a year up front costs less than ten monthly payments in every currency we bill in, so annual is more than two months free. It's the default on the Pro card above.
pricing.faq.cancel.a: Yes. Cancel from Settings → Billing. Your Pro access continues until the end of the billing period.

product.matchday.road.1.p: Each court is playing, called or free, with the match that is on it. A match with no court yet is listed too.
product.matchday.road.1.cap: Match Day on a phone: two pitches called, one free.
product.matchday.road.2.p: Pick a free court. It lists what is due there and what is waiting elsewhere. A court that is busy takes no call, and a match whose player is on another court is greyed out.
product.matchday.road.2.cap: A free pitch and the matches that could start there.

product.matchday.court.title: One phone per court. Every match streams itself.
product.matchday.court.lede: Link a court to your YouTube channel for the day and leave a phone on a tripod. Nobody presses record between matches.
product.matchday.court.1.p: Pick the court and your YouTube channel on the desk, then scan the court's code in {app}.
product.matchday.court.2.p: Each match on the court has a Stream switch. A match you leave off is never streamed.
product.matchday.court.3.p: Each match goes out as its own video with its own score on screen, and ends a few minutes after the result.
product.matchday.court.fig1: The phone on the tripod, ready for the match.
product.matchday.court.fig2: Start and stop by itself, with the health of the link.
product.matchday.ticket.title: The desk is free. Streams are per match.
product.matchday.ticket.body: One credit streams one match. A court that streams six matches uses six credits, and a match you do not stream costs nothing.
product.matchday.ticket.heading: On every plan
product.matchday.club.text: Seazn Demo Club runs a match day you can open: pitches, calls and live scores.
product.matchday.club.alt: Match Day on the web: two pitches called, one free, one match in play
product.matchday.faq.1.a: No. They scan one Match Day code in the Seazn Club Mobile App and get the day's matches.
product.matchday.faq.2.q: What if two people call the same court?
product.matchday.faq.2.a: A court with a match called or playing takes no other call, so the second person is told it is taken. A call can be undone.
product.matchday.faq.3.q: Are players told when their match is called?
product.matchday.faq.3.a: Not by Seazn. A call moves the match on the desk and on every volunteer's phone; you tell the players where to go. Planned times on the public schedule never move.
product.matchday.faq.4.a: No. Match Day works without it. Streaming is per match, when you want it.

product.registration.meta.title: Online registration and entry fees for competitions
product.registration.meta.description: Online registration for clubs and tournaments. Share one link, players enter and pay by card, and your entry list fills itself. Waiting list and refunds too.

product.registration.road.title: From a link to a full entry list
product.registration.road.lede: Three steps. Nobody types a name twice.
product.registration.road.1.h: Open entries and share the link
product.registration.road.1.p: Set who can enter, how many places there are and what it costs. Share the link, or print the QR code for the noticeboard.
product.registration.road.2.p: No account needed, just an email address. One sign-up can hold a whole squad or two children, paid in one go.
product.registration.road.3.p: Every entry lands in one list that shows who has paid. Confirmed entries are already in the division, ready for the draw.
product.registration.ticket.title: Taking entries is on every plan.
product.registration.ticket.body: Free entries and entries paid in cash cost you nothing. For entries paid by card, your plan sets our fee. Stripe's own card fee is separate, and the money goes straight to your club's Stripe account.
product.registration.ticket.heading: On each entry paid by card
product.registration.ticket.stubBottom: Free entries, cash and bank transfer.
product.registration.faq.1.q: What if a player does not pay?
product.registration.faq.1.a: A card entry left unpaid holds its place for {hours} hours. We email a reminder with a payment link before it runs out. After that the entry expires and the place goes to the next in line.
product.registration.faq.2.q: Can players pay by cash or bank transfer?
product.registration.faq.2.a: Yes. Choose Pay the organiser and write your own instructions. Each player sees their own reference to quote.
product.registration.faq.3.q: What happens when a division is full?
product.registration.faq.3.a: New entries join a waiting list and pay nothing. When someone withdraws, the first in line is offered the place and pays then.
product.registration.faq.4.a: A player who withdraws before your refund date is refunded in full, and our fee is returned too. After that date a refund is your decision.
product.registration.faq.5.q: Can someone enter without a team?
product.registration.faq.5.a: Yes, if you allow solo sign-ups. They wait in a pool, and you place each one in a team that has room.
product.registration.faq.6.a: Yes. Limit a division by category or by age. Under-18 divisions add a parent or guardian consent step.
